newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-Goodman sees double digit growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-Goodman sees double digit growth.

text.p: Australasian food group Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Friday it expected to boost profit before abnormal items by at least 10 percent in 1996/97, with the bulk of the gains to flow in the second half.
Managing director David Hearn told reporters after the annual meeting the first six months would be relatively flat.
"Certainly there will be a much stronger second half... because of the impact of wheat costs," Hearn said. Spot wheat prices have fallen 40 percent since May this year, he said.
Chairman David Clarke told the meeting Goodman would achieve "double digit growth in profit before abnormals" in 1996/97.

Hearn said the improvement would also be driven by higher sales prices, savings generated by taking advantage of the scale of Goodman's operations, and an increase in higher margin value-added products.
Goodman Fielder also announced it had secured a new chief financial officer and financial director following the surprise resignation in October of Les Cullen.
Clarke said the new appointee, who would be named within weeks, was an Australian from a top 50 company with experience in manufacturing.
Hearn said Goodman's earnings forecasts for 1996/97 were generally in line with those of market analysts.
BZW's Barcep survey of analysts has a median pre-abnormals profit forecast of about A$115 million for the 1996/97 year, about 15 percent up on the A$100.7 million recorded in 1995/96.
On a divisional basis, Hearn said milling/baking was expected to recover, especially in the second half after an eight percent fall in operating profit last year to A$8.1 million.
Cereals and snacks would generate an improved result on the back of higher sales, lower wheat prices and cost controls.
The edible oils and food service division was expected to produce a similar result to the A$41.1 million posted in 1995/96.

Hearn said he was confident of major progress in the poultry division, while Clarke said later the operation could match or even better its 1994/95 operating profit of A$15.1 million after falling to A$9.6 million in 1995/96.
However the European foods division was expected to struggle to improve on the A$48.5 million profit generated in 1995/96.

"Aggressive competition in the bakeries business ... combined with higher European wheat costs will put this business under pressure this year and we will probably not match last year's performance," Hearn said.
The ingredients division would perform strongly while the international division would also grow significantly after strong sales in China in 1995/96.
Goodman also indicated it would be some time before the company focused on acquisitions or divestments.
"Our task at hand at the moment is to optimise the portfolio we have," Hearn said. "That means we are not primarily looking to sell businesses, nor are we primarily looking to buy them."
Hearn said the company had "another year or 18 months of solid work" ahead but should be able to make a "significant strategic move" in two years' time if it wanted to.
Goodman Fielder shares at 3.25 p.m. (0425 GMT) were three cents stronger at A$1.50. The stock has traded between A$1.20 and A$1.54 over the past year.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
